mainTopic: Conditional גיטין: the sick husband's גט, and a גט or קידושין 'on condition' of payment (רב הונא vs. רב יהודה)
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ברייתא about a sick husband who gives a גט that works only if he dies. רבי יהודה says that until then she is fully his wife. רבי מאיר says her relations with another man are 'hanging'. רבי יוסי says they are a ספק. חכמים say she is 'divorced and not divorced'. The גמרא explains that רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי differ over an אשם תלוי, and that חכמים differ from רבי יוסי over the husband's duty to support her. A new משנה then teaches a גט given 'on condition that you give me two hundred זוז', the same condition with a thirty-day deadline, and the lost-coat case in צידן. רב הונא says the divorce works now and she must still pay. רב יהודה says it works only once she pays. They hold the same views about קידושין, and the גמרא explains why both cases had to be taught. A ברייתא seems to refute רב יהודה, and he answers that it follows רבי while he follows the רבנן. רבי זירא then reports that רבי יוחנן said everyone agrees 'על מנת' is like 'מעכשיו', which undercuts that answer.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: until he dies, she is fully his wife
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes רבי יהודה's view. While the sick husband is still alive, the woman is treated as his wife in every way. The only difference is that she will not need a second גט if he dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he becomes impure for her. The general rule is: she is like his wife in every way, except that she does not need a second גט from him. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא is finishing רבי יהודה's list of ways this woman is still treated as a wife, and then sums it all up in one rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though she already holds a conditional גט, רבי יהודה says nothing changes for now: he can become טמא for her like any husband. The one real effect of the גט is that, if he dies from this illness, the divorce already given is enough and no new גט is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Becomes ritually impure (here, a כהן who may become impure for a close relative's burial)
The general rule of the matter, a summary line
Like his wife in every respect

phrases.english: And he becomes impure for her.
phrases.notes: If he is a כהן, he may become טמא for her burial, the way a husband may for his wife.

phrases.english: The general rule of the matter is:
She is like his wife in every way,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא שֶׁאֵינָהּ צְרִיכָה הֵימֶנּוּ גֵּט שֵׁנִי,
phrases.english: except that she does not need a second גט from him,
These are the words of רבי יהודה.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּלָלוֹ שֶׁל דָּבָר: הֲרֵי הִיא כְּאִשְׁתּוֹ לְכׇל דָּבָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא's ongoing list (from before this section) of how she is treated as his wife.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Per רבי יהודה, until the husband dies she is his wife in every way; the conditional גט only spares her from needing a second גט later.

steps.title: Three other views: hanging, doubtful, or divorced-and-not-divorced
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר says that if she is with another man in the meantime, the status of that act is 'hanging' until we know what happens. רבי יוסי says it is a ספק. חכמים say she is 'divorced and not divorced,' but only if he actually dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר says: her relations are hanging. רבי יוסי says: her relations are in doubt. And חכמים say: she is divorced and not divorced, provided that he dies.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings three more opinions about her status during the waiting period, especially if she is with another man.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר's word 'hanging' means the answer will become clear later: if he dies from this illness, the divorce counts and the act was not adultery. רבי יוסי's word 'doubt' suggests the question may never be fully settled. חכמים call her 'divorced and not divorced,' and that doubt exists only if he dies; if he lives, she was never divorced.

keyTerms.meaning: Her act of relations (here, with another man)
Hanging, waiting to be decided by what happens later
Divorced and not divorced, a doubtful status

steps.confusionAlert: 'Hanging' (רבי מאיר) and 'doubt' (רבי יוסי) sound almost the same. The difference is that 'hanging' will get a clear answer later, while 'doubt' can stay unresolved. That is exactly what the גמרא asks about next.

phrases.english: רבי מאיר says:
Her relations are hanging.
phrases.notes: Whether her being with another man counts as being with a married woman waits on whether her husband dies from this illness.

phrases.english: רבי יוסי says: her relations are in doubt.
And the Sages say:
She is divorced and not divorced,
provided that he dies.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives views that differ from רבי יהודה's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: her relations are 'hanging.' רבי יוסי: they are 'doubtful.' חכמים: she is 'divorced and not divorced,' and only if he dies.

steps.title: What is the difference between רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between 'hanging' and 'doubt.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What difference is there between רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion with a clarifying question and sets up the next step, where an answer will be given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two terms sound so close that we need to know whether they lead to any different practical law. The גמרא wants a concrete case where the two opinions would rule differently.

phrases.english: What difference is there between
רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אִיכָּא בֵּין רַבִּי מֵאִיר לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the two similar-sounding opinions in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical legal difference between 'hanging' (רבי מאיר) and 'doubt' (רבי יוסי).

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the difference is an אשם תלוי
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that the difference is whether the other man brings an אשם תלוי. According to רבי מאיר he does not; according to רבי יוסי he does.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: the difference between them is an אשם תלוי. According to רבי מאיר, he does not bring an אשם תלוי. According to רבי יוסי, he does bring an אשם תלוי.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a practical case where 'hanging' and 'doubt' lead to different laws: whether the other man must bring an אשם תלוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אשם תלוי is brought by someone unsure whether he did a sin that would require a חטאת. For רבי מאיר the doubt will be cleared up later, once the husband dies or gets better, so there is no lasting doubt and no אשם תלוי. For רבי יוסי the doubt stays, even if he dies, since it is unclear when the גט took effect, so the man brings an אשם תלוי.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'suspended' guilt-offering, brought when one is unsure whether he sinned
There is a difference between them

steps.whatToRemember: 'Hanging' (רבי מאיר) means the answer will come later, so no אשם תלוי. 'Doubt' (רבי יוסי) means it stays uncertain, so the man brings an אשם תלוי.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that two words that sound almost the same can have real halachic results. A doubt that will be resolved later is not the same as a doubt that stays forever.

phrases.english: רבי יוחנן said:
The difference between them is an אשם תלוי;
phrases.notes: This is the offering for someone unsure whether he did a sin that would need a חטאת (ויקרא 5:17-19).

phrases.aramaic: לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר – לָא מַיְיתֵי אָשָׁם תָּלוּי,
phrases.english: According to רבי מאיר, he does not bring an אשם תלוי,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the other man who was with her.

phrases.english: and according to רבי יוסי, he does bring an אשם תלוי.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אָשָׁם תָּלוּי אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The practical difference is the אשם תלוי. Under רבי מאיר the doubt will be resolved later, so none is brought; under רבי יוסי the doubt stays, so one is brought.

steps.title: Aren't חכמים saying the same thing as רבי יוסי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the חכמים line of the ברייתא again and asks how their view differs from רבי יוסי's.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא said: 'And חכמים say: she is divorced and not divorced.' But that is just what רבי יוסי said!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the last opinion in the ברייתא and points out that it sounds the same as רבי יוסי's. It is setting up the next step, which will show the difference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי called the status a ספק, a doubt. חכמים said 'divorced and not divorced,' which also sounds like a doubt. If both mean the same thing, why does the ברייתא list them as two separate opinions?

keyTerms.meaning: 'Divorced and not divorced,' a status that is unclear either way
'That is the same as,' used to say two opinions look identical

phrases.english: And the Sages say: she is divorced and not divorced.
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quoting again the last line of the ברייתא from step 2, so it can ask about it.

phrases.english: The Sages are the same as Rabbi Yosei!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 4 showed how רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי differ. Now the גמרא asks the same question about רבי יוסי and חכמים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical difference is there between רבי יוסי's 'doubt' and חכמים' 'divorced and not divorced'?

steps.title: The difference is the husband's duty to support her
steps.stepSummary: The difference between the two views is a rule of שמואל: wherever חכמים say 'divorced and not divorced,' the husband must still pay for his wife's food.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference between them: the rule of רבי זירא. רבי זירא said in the name of רבה בר ירמיה, who said in the name of שמואל: Wherever חכמים said 'divorced and not divorced,' her husband must still provide her food.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two opinions do differ in practice. The difference is whether the husband still has to support his wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's rule is tied to the exact phrase חכמים use, 'divorced and not divorced.' That phrase means the husband still owes his wife support, but רבי יוסי's wording, 'doubt,' does not carry this rule. So the two opinions are not the same after all.

keyTerms.meaning: 'There is a difference between them,' introducing the practical result of a dispute
'Wherever,' a general rule that applies every time
Food and support a husband owes his wife

steps.whatToRemember: חכמים' phrase 'divorced and not divorced' is not just another way of saying ספק. According to שמואל, it means the husband still has to support his wife.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them: the rule of Rabbi Zeira.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר יִרְמְיָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: As Rabbi Zeira said that Rabba bar Yirmeya said that Shmuel said:
Wherever the Sages said
'she is divorced and not divorced,'
her husband is obligated to provide her food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 5 by naming a practical difference.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The difference is שמואל's rule that wherever חכמים say 'divorced and not divorced,' the husband must support his wife.

steps.title: A divorce on condition that she pays two hundred זוז
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: if a husband gives a גט on condition that his wife pay him two hundred זוז, she is divorced and must pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If he says, 'Here is your גט, on condition that you give me two hundred זוז,' she is divorced, and she must pay.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It deals with a גט that comes with a money condition and no deadline.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband attaches a condition to the גט, and the משנה rules that she is divorced. She still has to pay the two hundred זוז, because the condition is part of the deal.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה, marking the start of a new משנה
'On condition that,' attaching a requirement to an act
Two hundred זוז, a sum of money

phrases.english: MISHNA: 'Here is your bill of divorce,'

phrases.aramaic: עַל מְנָת שֶׁתִּתְּנִי לִי מָאתַיִם זוּז״ –
phrases.english: 'on condition that you give me two hundred zuz' –
she is divorced, and she must give it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲרֵי זֶה גִּיטִּךְ, עַל מְנָת שֶׁתִּתְּנִי לִי מָאתַיִם זוּז
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic. The new משנה starts here.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גט given on condition of paying two hundred זוז, with no deadline, makes her divorced, and she must pay.

steps.title: The same condition with a thirty-day deadline
steps.stepSummary: If the husband sets a thirty-day deadline for the payment, she is divorced only if she pays within that time.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he says, 'On condition that you give me the money from now until thirty days,' and she pays within thirty days, she is divorced. If not, she is not divorced.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with a second case. This time the money condition has a deadline.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Adding a time limit changes the result. Paying on time makes the divorce work. Missing the deadline means the divorce never takes effect.

keyTerms.meaning: 'From now until,' setting a time limit

phrases.english: 'On condition that you give me'
phrases.notes: He means the same two hundred זוז from the case just before.

phrases.english: 'from now until thirty days' –

phrases.aramaic: אִם נָתְנָה לוֹ בְּתוֹךְ שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם, מְגוֹרֶשֶׁת;
phrases.english: if she gave it to him within thirty days, she is divorced;
and if not, she is not divorced.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַל מְנָת שֶׁתִּתְּנִי לִי מִיכָּן וְעַד שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a time limit to the condition in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With a thirty-day deadline, the divorce works only if she pays within thirty days.

steps.title: The lost coat in צידן
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל tells of a husband who made the גט depend on his wife giving him his coat. She lost it, and חכמים ruled that she may give him its value instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said: There was a case in צידן. A man said to his wife, 'Here is your גט, on condition that you give me my coat.' The coat was lost, and חכמים said: she should give him its value.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a real case. The condition was to return a specific item, and that item was lost.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In plain words, the husband asked for his actual coat. Since it was gone, she could not give it back. Even so, חכמים ruled that paying its value counts as meeting the condition.

keyTerms.meaning: A real incident brought as a precedent

steps.whyThisMatters: This case raises the question of whether the husband's condition meant the exact item or just its worth.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said:
There was an incident in Tzaidan, with one who said to his wife:

phrases.aramaic: ״הֲרֵי זֶה גִּיטִּךְ, עַל מְנָת שֶׁתִּתְּנִי לִי אִיצְטְלִיתִי״,
phrases.english: 'Here is your bill of divorce, on condition that you give me my coat,'
and his coat was lost,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרוּ חֲכָמִים: תִּתֵּן לוֹ אֶת דָּמֶיהָ.
phrases.english: and the Sages said: she should give him its value.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from conditions about money to a condition about a specific item that no longer exists.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the item in the condition is lost, she may pay its value and so meet the condition.

steps.title: What does 'and she must give' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins discussing the משנה and asks what the word וְתִתֵּן means.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What does 'and she must give' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its discussion of the משנה from step 7 by asking what 'and she must give' means. This line sets up the two answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said she is divorced 'and she must give' the two hundred זוז. It is not clear whether the divorce works now and the payment comes later, or whether the divorce waits for the payment. The גמרא wants to pin down the timing.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה

phrases.english: Gemara:
What is meant by 'and she must give'?
phrases.notes: These words come from the משנה in step 7: she is divorced and must pay him two hundred זוז.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's discussion of the משנה quoted in step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the divorce takes effect right away or only once she pays.

steps.title: רב הונא and רב יהודה disagree on the meaning
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא: she is divorced now and must pay. רב יהודה: she is divorced only once she pays.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא says: and she must give. רב יהודה says: when she gives.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give two different readings of 'and she must give.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב הונא, the divorce works right away and the payment is something she still has to do. For רב יהודה, the divorce only takes effect at the moment she pays.
steps.confusionAlert: רב הונא does not say she can skip paying. In both views she must pay. They only argue about when the divorce takes effect.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said: and she must give.
phrases.notes: He means she is divorced right now, and the payment is still owed.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said: when she gives.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10 with two opinions.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב הונא: she is divorced immediately and must pay. רב יהודה: the divorce takes effect only when she pays.

steps.title: What is the practical difference between them?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the two views differ in practice.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a case where the two opinions would lead to a different ruling. It is setting up the answer that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both views, once she pays she is divorced. So the גמרא looks for a case where the timing actually changes the result.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical result of the מחלוקת in step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where the two views give different rulings.

steps.title: A torn or lost גט before she pays
steps.stepSummary: If the גט is torn or lost before she pays, רב הונא says she needs no second גט. רב יהודה says she does.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference is when the גט was torn or lost. רב הונא, who says 'and she must give,' holds she does not need a second גט from him. רב יהודה, who says 'when she gives,' holds she needs a second גט from him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the difference is a גט that was torn or lost after she got it but before she paid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב הונא, the גט already worked when she received it, so once she pays, its later loss does not matter. For רב יהודה, the divorce happens only at payment. By then the גט is gone, so there is nothing to divorce her and she needs a new one.
steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא: the גט works now, so its later loss doesn't matter. רב יהודה: the גט works only at payment, so it must still exist then.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them
where the get was torn or lost;
phrases.notes: This happened after she received the גט but before she paid.

phrases.english: Rav Huna, who says 'and she must give' —
she does not need a second get from him;
Rav Yehuda, who says 'when she gives' —
she needs a second get from him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ שֶׁנִּתְקָרַע הַגֵּט אוֹ שֶׁאָבַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 12 with a practical case.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A torn or lost גט: no second גט according to רב הונא, a second גט according to רב יהודה.

steps.title: The same wording appears in a משנה about קידושין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה: if a man is מקדש a woman on condition that he gives her two hundred זוז, she is מקודשת and he must give.
steps.simpleTranslation: We also learned something like this about קידושין: if a man says to a woman, 'You are מקודשת to me on condition that I give you two hundred זוז,' she is מקודשת, and he must give.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that a משנה about קידושין uses the very same wording. It is setting up the parallel מחלוקת that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the man makes the condition about himself paying, not the woman. The words 'and he must give' raise the same question about timing.

keyTerms.meaning: And we also learned (in a משנה)

phrases.english: And we also learned regarding betrothal
a case like this —
as we learned: one who says to a woman:
'You are hereby betrothed to me,

phrases.aramaic: עַל מְנָת שֶׁאֶתֵּן לִיךְ מָאתַיִם זוּז״ –
phrases.english: on condition that I give you two hundred zuz' —
she is betrothed, and he must give.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּתְנַן נָמֵי גַּבֵּי קִידּוּשִׁין כִּי הַאי גַוְונָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a parallel case with the same wording.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman given קידושין on condition that he pays two hundred זוז is מקודשת, and he must pay.

steps.title: The same מחלוקת about 'and he must give'
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא and רב יהודה argue in the same way: is she מקודשת now, or only when he pays?
steps.simpleTranslation: It was said: what does 'and he must give' mean? רב הונא said: and he must give. רב יהודה said: when he gives.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports that רב הונא and רב יהודה had the same argument about the קידושין משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב הונא, the קידושין take effect right away and the payment is owed. For רב יהודה, the קידושין take effect only when he pays. Each אמורא stays consistent with his view on the גט.

phrases.english: And it was said: what is meant by 'and he must give'?
Rav Huna said: and he must give.
Rav Yehuda said: when he gives.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the אמוראים' dispute over the משנה quoted in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב הונא: she is מקודשת now and he must pay. רב יהודה: she is מקודשת only when he pays.

steps.title: What is the practical difference in קידושין?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the two views differ in the קידושין case.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא again asks for a practical case where the two views differ, this time for קידושין. It is setting up the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The torn-גט case does not apply here, so the גמרא needs a different case that shows the effect of the timing.

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical result of the מחלוקת in step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where the two views differ about קידושין.

steps.title: She accepted קידושין from another man before he paid
steps.stepSummary: If she accepted קידושין from someone else before the first man paid: for רב הונא the first קידושין already hold, so the second ones do not work. For רב יהודה the first קידושין have not taken effect yet, so the second ones work.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference is where she reached out her hand and accepted קידושין from another man. רב הונא, who says 'and he must give,' holds it is just a condition: he fulfills his condition and goes on. רב יהודה, who says 'when he gives,' holds that only once he gives her the money are they קידושין, but right now they are not קידושין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the difference is a woman who accepts קידושין from a second man before the first man pays.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב הונא, the payment is just a condition he has to keep. She is already מקודשת to the first man, so the second man's קידושין do nothing. For רב יהודה, the first קידושין begin only at payment. Right now she is free, so the second man's קידושין take effect.

keyTerms.meaning: She reached out her hand (to accept)
He fulfills his condition and goes on

steps.whatToRemember: In both the גט and קידושין cases, רב הונא says the act works right away and the payment is owed. רב יהודה says the act works only once payment is made.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them —
where she reached out her hand
and accepted betrothal from another man.
phrases.notes: This happened before the first man paid the two hundred זוז.

phrases.english: Rav Huna, who says 'and he must give' —
it is merely a condition,
he fulfills his condition and goes on.
phrases.notes: In other words, she is already his, so the second man's קידושין don't work.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda, who says 'when he gives' —

phrases.aramaic: לְכִי יָהֵיב לַהּ הוּא דְּהָווּ קִידּוּשִׁין,
phrases.english: only when he gives it to her is it betrothal,
right now it is not betrothal.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ שֶׁפָּשְׁטָה יָדָהּ וְקִיבְּלָה קִידּוּשִׁין מֵאַחֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 16 with a practical case.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: If she accepted קידושין from another man before payment: according to רב הונא the second קידושין fail; according to רב יהודה they take effect.

steps.title: Why רב הונא's view must be stated for divorce too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says both cases are needed. If we only had קידושין, we might think רב הונא says 'it works now' only because the man wants to bring her close. In divorce he wants to push her away, so maybe רב הונא would agree with רב יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is necessary to state both cases. If we had only been told about קידושין, we might say that only there רב הונא rules 'it works now, and he must give,' because the man wants to bring her close. But in a divorce, where he is pushing her away, we might say רב הונא agrees with רב יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a צריכותא, explaining why the same argument is taught twice. This first part shows why we need the divorce case to know רב הונא's real view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A man who is marrying a woman is happy to do it, so his condition probably means 'it takes effect now, pay later.' A man divorcing his wife may not be happy about it, so we might think he wants the divorce delayed until she pays. The divorce case teaches that רב הונא says 'it works now' even there.

keyTerms.meaning: It is necessary (to teach both cases)
He comes to bring her close (to marry her)
He comes to push her away (to divorce her)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new argument. The גמרא is only explaining why the same argument had to be told for both קידושין and גירושין.

phrases.english: And it is necessary;
for if it had taught us only about betrothal,
[we would say] in this case Rav Huna says 'and he must give' –
phrases.notes: Meaning: the קידושין take effect right away, and he still has to pay.

phrases.english: because he comes to bring her close;
but regarding divorce, where he comes to push her away,
I might say he agrees with Rav Yehuda;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After showing the same argument in גירושין and קידושין, the גמרא explains why both are needed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The divorce case is needed to show that רב הונא says 'it works now' even when the husband is pushing her away.

steps.title: Why רב הונא's view must be stated for betrothal too
steps.stepSummary: If we only had the divorce case, we might think רב הונא says 'it works now' only because the husband is not embarrassed to ask her for the money later. In קידושין, the woman is embarrassed to ask him for it, so maybe רב הונא would agree with רב יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if we had only been told about divorce, we might say that only there רב הונא rules 'it works now, and she must give,' because the husband is not embarrassed to ask her for the money. But in קידושין, where she is embarrassed to ask him for it, we might say רב הונא agrees with רב יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the צריכותא from the other side. It shows why we need the קידושין case to know רב הונא's real view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A husband can easily ask his ex-wife for the money she owes, so he lets the גט work now. A woman may feel too shy to chase a man for money he promised, so she might want the קידושין to wait until he pays. The קידושין case teaches that רב הונא still says 'it works now.'

keyTerms.meaning: And she must give (the divorce works now, and she still pays)

phrases.english: And if it had taught us only about divorce;
[we would say] in this case Rav Huna says 'and she must give' –
because he is not embarrassed to demand it from her;
but regarding betrothal, where she is embarrassed to demand it from him,
I might say he agrees with Rav Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The mirror image of step 18: now the קידושין case is shown to be needed for רב הונא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The קידושין case is needed to show that רב הונא says 'it works now' even when the woman would be embarrassed to demand payment.

steps.title: Why רב יהודה's view must be stated for divorce too
steps.stepSummary: Now the גמרא turns to רב יהודה. If we only had קידושין, we might think he says 'only when he pays' because the woman is embarrassed to ask for the money. In divorce the husband is not embarrassed to ask, so maybe רב יהודה would agree with רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if we had only been told about קידושין, we might say that only there רב יהודה rules 'only once he gives,' because she is embarrassed to ask him for the money. But in a divorce, where the husband is not embarrassed to ask her, we might say רב יהודה agrees with רב הונא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now uses the same two reasons to explain why both cases are needed for רב יהודה's view. This step shows why we need the divorce case for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same 'embarrassment' reason from step 19 is now turned around. For רב יהודה, the shy woman explains why קידושין would wait for payment. But a husband can easily collect, so we might think the גט works right away. The divorce case teaches that רב יהודה still says 'only once she pays.'

keyTerms.meaning: Once he gives (it takes effect only when he pays)

phrases.english: And if it had taught us only about betrothal;
[we would say] in this case Rav Yehuda says 'once he gives' –
because she is embarrassed to demand it from him;

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל גַּבֵּי גֵירוּשִׁין – דְּלָא כְּסִיף לְמִיתְבְּעַהּ,
phrases.english: but regarding divorce, where he is not embarrassed to demand it from her,
I might say he agrees with Rav Huna;

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אַשְׁמְעִינַן גַּבֵּי קִידּוּשִׁין; בְּהָא קָאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the embarrassment reason from step 19, now from רב יהודה's side.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The divorce case is needed to show that רב יהודה says 'only once she pays' even though the husband could easily collect.

steps.title: Why רב יהודה's view must be stated for betrothal too, so both cases are needed
steps.stepSummary: If we only had divorce, we might think רב יהודה says 'only when she pays' because the husband is pushing her away. In קידושין he wants her close, so maybe רב יהודה would agree with רב הונא. So both cases are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if we had only been told about divorce, we might say that only there רב יהודה rules 'only once she gives,' because the husband is pushing her away. But in קידושין, where he wants to bring her close, we might say רב יהודה agrees with רב הונא. So both cases are necessary.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the last of the four reasons and then closes with 'צריכא': both cases really are needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'close vs. far' reason from step 18 is now turned around for רב יהודה. A husband pushing his wife away might want to delay, but a man marrying her would want it to work now. The קידושין case shows that רב יהודה still says 'only once he pays,' so each אמורא holds his view in both cases.

keyTerms.meaning: Once she gives (the divorce takes effect only when she pays)
I might say (a possible mistaken thought)

steps.whatToRemember: Two reasons drive the צריכותא: (1) close vs. far: a man marrying wants it now, a man divorcing may want delay; (2) embarrassment: a husband easily asks for money, a woman may be too shy. Each reason could have made רב הונא or רב יהודה give in for one case, so both cases are needed to show each one holds his view everywhere.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the argument is not about the special feelings in marriage or divorce. It is a general argument about what 'on condition' means: does it work now, or only once the condition is done?

phrases.english: And if it had taught us only about divorce;
[we would say] in this case Rav Yehuda says 'once she gives' –
because he comes to push her away;
but regarding betrothal, where he comes to bring her close,
I might say he agrees with Rav Huna;
[Therefore] it is necessary [to state both].

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אַשְׁמְעִינַן גַּבֵּי גֵירוּשִׁין; בְּהָא קָאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the fourth and last reason and closes the צריכותא that began in step 18.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both the גט case and the קידושין case are needed, because each could have led one אמורא to agree with the other; stating both shows that רב הונא and רב יהודה each hold their view in all cases.

steps.title: A ברייתא: the גט works even if it was torn or lost
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב יהודה with a ברייתא. A גט given 'on condition that you give me 200 זוז' works even if the paper was torn or lost before she paid. She may not remarry until she pays.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: 'Here is your גט on condition that you give me two hundred זוז.' Even if the גט got torn or lost, she is divorced. But she may not marry another man until she pays.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that seems to go against רב יהודה. The full challenge is built over the next two steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the גט only took effect when she paid, a torn or lost גט should be a problem, because by then there would be no גט. The ברייתא says she is still divorced, so the גט must have worked when he handed it to her. That is רב הונא's view. Paying the money just completes the condition.

keyTerms.meaning: A silver coin (the same as a דינר)

steps.confusionAlert: She is divorced, yet she still may not remarry until she pays. Until she pays, the condition is not yet fulfilled, so the divorce is not yet final.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
'This is your bill of divorce,

phrases.aramaic: עַל מְנָת שֶׁתִּתְּנִי לִי מָאתַיִם זוּז״,
phrases.english: on condition that you give me two hundred zuz,'

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁנִּקְרַע הַגֵּט אוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱבַד
phrases.english: even though the bill of divorce was torn or lost
she is divorced;
but she may not marry another man
until she gives the money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After showing that both cases of the מחלוקת are needed, the גמרא now challenges רב יהודה's side.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's view that 'on condition' takes effect only when the condition is fulfilled.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A גט that no longer exists when she pays still works. So it must have taken effect when it was handed over.

steps.title: Second part of the ברייתא: the husband died before she paid
steps.stepSummary: In the same ברייתא, if the husband died childless: if she had already paid, she is free of the יבם. If she had not paid, she is bound to the יבם. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says she can pay his father, brother or another relative.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught: 'Here is your גט on condition that you give me two hundred זוז,' and he died. If she had paid, she does not need the יבם. If she had not paid, she needs the יבם. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: she gives the money to his father, his brother, or one of the relatives.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second ruling from the same ברייתא to strengthen the challenge. The next step draws the conclusion from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל lets her pay after the husband is dead, and that frees her. A divorce cannot begin after the husband dies. So her paying must make the גט count from back when it was given.

keyTerms.meaning: Bound to the husband's brother (needs יבום or חליצה)

phrases.english: And it is taught further:
'This is your bill of divorce,

phrases.aramaic: עַל מְנָת שֶׁתִּתְּנִי לִי מָאתַיִם זוּז״, וָמֵת,
phrases.english: on condition that you give me two hundred zuz,' and he died,
phrases.notes: He died with no children. That is why his brother, the יבם, comes into the picture.

phrases.english: if she had given, she is not bound to the yavam;
if she had not given, she is bound to the yavam.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
She gives it to his father or to his brother
or to one of the relatives.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second ruling from the same ברייתא to the challenge.
steps.raayaObject: That a condition with 'on condition' works from the time the גט was given (רב הונא's view).
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about the husband who died before she paid, with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's view that 'on condition' takes effect only when the condition is fulfilled.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל lets her pay the heirs after the husband's death and so be freed. A divorce cannot begin after death, so the payment must make the גט work from when it was given.

steps.title: Both opinions treat it as a real condition, so רב יהודה seems refuted
steps.stepSummary: The first תנא and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל argue only about whether 'to me' includes the heirs. Both agree this is a condition that makes the גט work from the start. That seems to refute רב יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They argue only about this: one holds 'to me' means not to my heirs, and the other holds 'to me' means even to my heirs. But everyone agrees it is a condition. This is a refutation of רב יהודה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the conclusion from the ברייתא. Both תנאים agree with רב הונא, so רב יהודה looks refuted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only argument is about who may receive the money. Nobody argues about how the condition works. For both, paying fulfills a תנאי on a גט that was already given, so the divorce works from the start. That is the opposite of רב יהודה, who says it starts only when she pays.

keyTerms.meaning: They only argue about this much

phrases.english: They disagree only about this:
one Sage holds 'to me' means and not to my heirs,
phrases.notes: This 'one Sage' is the first תנא in the ברייתא.

phrases.english: and the other Sage holds 'to me' means even to my heirs;
phrases.notes: This one is רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

phrases.english: but in any event, everyone agrees it is a condition
this is a refutation of Rav Yehuda!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the ברייתא quoted in the last two steps.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both תנאים agree that 'on condition' is a תנאי on a גט that already took effect, so nobody holds like רב יהודה.

steps.title: רב יהודה: the ברייתא follows רבי, and I hold like the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה answers that the ברייתא follows רבי, who says 'on condition' is like 'from now'. The רבנן disagree with רבי, and רב יהודה rules like the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה can tell you: Whose view is this? It is רבי's. As רב הונא said in the name of רבי: anyone who says 'on condition' is like one who says 'from now'. The רבנן disagree with him, and I rule like the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה defends himself. The ברייתא is not a problem for him, because it follows one side of an older מחלוקת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה admits the ברייתא follows רב הונא's view. But he shows that this view belongs to רבי, and the רבנן argue with רבי. Since רב יהודה follows the רבנן, a ברייתא that follows רבי cannot refute him.

keyTerms.meaning: He can tell you (introduces a defense)

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא's view, that 'on condition' works from now, is רבי's view. רב יהודה's view, that it works only once the condition is fulfilled, follows the רבנן who argue with רבי. So a ברייתא that follows רבי cannot refute רב יהודה.
steps.confusionAlert: The רב הונא quoted here is passing on רבי's teaching. This is what matches him with רבי's side of the argument.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda could say to you:
Whose view is this? It is Rabbi's,
as Rav Huna said that Rabbi said:
anyone who says 'on condition'
is like one who says 'from now.'
And the Rabbis disagree with him,
and I say my ruling following the Rabbis.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the refutation brought against רב יהודה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributes the ברייתא to one side of a תנאים מחלוקת (רבי), while רב יהודה follows the other side (רבנן).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Everyone agrees that 'on condition' works from the moment the גט was given, so רב יהודה stands alone.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only רבי holds that 'on condition' is like 'from now'. The רבנן disagree, and רב יהודה follows them.

steps.title: What they used to say in בבל
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא reports that in בבל they understood the רבנן to disagree with רבי's rule that 'על מנת' is like 'מעכשיו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: When we were in בבל, we used to say that the רבנן disagree with רבי's rule, which רב הונא quoted, that saying 'על מנת' is like saying 'מעכשיו'.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא tells us how the scholars in בבל understood רבי's rule. This sets up a contrast with what he will hear in ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The view of בבל matches what רב יהודה just said in Step 25: the רבנן argue with רבי about 'על מנת'. If that were the final word, רב יהודה's answer would stand firmly. The next step will challenge this understanding.

keyTerms.meaning: 'On condition that'. Wording that attaches a condition to a גט or other act
'From now'. The act takes effect right away, once the condition is later fulfilled
The Sages, the majority view arguing against רבי

phrases.english: And Rabbi Zeira said:
When we were in Babylonia, we would say,

phrases.aramaic: הָא דְּאָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַבִּי:
phrases.english: regarding this that Rav Huna said in the name of Rebbi:
phrases.notes: 'רבי' with no name means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: anyone who says 'on condition'
is like one who says 'from now',
the Rabbis disagree with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: כִּי הֲוֵינַן בְּבָבֶל אָמְרִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reports a tradition from בבל that fits רב יהודה's claim in Step 25 that the רבנן argue with רבי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In בבל they held that the רבנן disagree with רבי's rule that 'על מנת' equals 'מעכשיו'.

steps.title: In ארץ ישראל: everyone agrees about 'on condition'
steps.stepSummary: In ארץ ישראל, רבי אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן that all agree 'על מנת' is like 'מעכשיו'. The argument is only about 'מהיום ולאחר מיתה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: When I went up to ארץ ישראל, I found רבי אסי sitting and saying in the name of רבי יוחנן: Everyone agrees that one who says 'על מנת' is like one who says 'מעכשיו'. They only argued about 'מהיום ולאחר מיתה' (from today and after death).
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא reports that in ארץ ישראל they had a different tradition. There, nobody argues with רבי about 'על מנת'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יוחנן, the רבנן agree with רבי that 'על מנת' works like 'מעכשיו'. Their argument is about a different wording: 'מהיום ולאחר מיתה'. This weakens רב יהודה's answer from Step 25, because he relied on the רבנן disagreeing about 'על מנת'.

keyTerms.meaning: I went up, meaning to ארץ ישראל
'From today and after death'. A different wording, and the real subject of the argument

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two wordings. According to רבי יוחנן, there is no argument about 'על מנת'. The argument is only about 'מהיום ולאחר מיתה'.
steps.whyThisMatters: רב יהודה's answer depended on the רבנן disagreeing with רבי about 'על מנת'. רבי יוחנן's tradition says they do not.

phrases.english: When I went up,
phrases.notes: He means when he moved up from בבל to ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: I found Rabbi Asi
sitting and saying
in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
Everyone agrees that one who says 'on condition'
is like one who says 'from now'.
They argued only
about 'from today and after death'.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי סְלִיקִי, אַשְׁכַּחְתֵּיהּ לְרַבִּי אַסִּי דְּיָתֵיב וְקָאָמַר מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with the tradition from בבל in Step 26 and undercuts the base of רב יהודה's answer in Step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's answer (Step 25) that the רבנן disagree with רבי about 'על מנת'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן says everyone, including the רבנן, agrees that 'על מנת' is like 'מעכשיו'. So there is no רבנן view against the ברייתא for רב יהודה to follow.
